newsitem.title: USA: TCI Satellite may be hurt by new EchoStar deal.
newsitem.headline: TCI Satellite may be hurt by new EchoStar deal.

text.p: TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc (TSAT) is more vulnerable than other direct-broadcast satellite (DBS) companies to increased competition from the new alliance between EchoStar Communications Corp and News Corp, some high-yield analysts said.

"At the end of the day, competitive pressures on EchoStar will be greater than before -- especially since they have the least amount of spectrum amongst all the DBS vendors," said G. Robert Berzins, high-yield analyst at Lehman Brothers Inc.
TSAT junk bonds initially rallied Tuesday morning, but lost most of their gains in late trading, traders said.
TSAT 10.875 percent senior subordinated notes due '06 were trading at 102-102 1/8 late on Tuesday, up only 1/4 of a point from pre-announcement levels.
Late on Monday, News Corp said it would buy 50 percent of EchoStar in a deal valued at $1 billion.
News Corp said it would combine the satellite assets of its American Sky Broadcasting venture with EchoStar to creating an even stronger competitor in the DBS market known an as "Sky."
Industry experts said the combined company will control over twice the number of high-frequency DBS satellite transponders as TSAT.
This will allow the new Sky service to provide up to 500 channels, compared to 100-150 channels on TSAT, they said.
Lehman's Berzins says Sky will also put more pressure on DBS companies to provide local television channels, which could put TSAT's PRIMESTAR DBS product at a disadvantage.
PRIMESTAR, which is a joint venture between TSAT and the largest cable companies, does not provide local programming currently.
A TSAT spokeswoman disagreed, saying these factors were not significant because TSAT had a more customized, niche strategy than its competitors.

She said Sky's emphasis on local programming "was further support" of TSAT's new "Cable Plus" product would allow cable companies to supplement their cable service with a DBS product, all through one unit.
The new service, which is expected to be rolled out by mid-fall, would provide customers with local channels via existing cable lines as well as up to 100 extra channels via a DBS dish, she said.
"The quantity of channels available (via Cable Plus) will be ample for the service we want to provide. It will focus on what customers feel is the most valuable part of the satellite package."

The TSAT spokeswoman said the EchoStar/News Corp alliance was also a positive for TSAT becuase it would reduce the number of DBS competitors from four to three, as well as "reinforce strategic thinking about value of investing in this growth industry and being an investment in long term."
DirecTV, owned by Hughes Electronics Inc, is the only other major DBS provider other than PRIMESTAR and the new SKY service.
Berzins agreed having fewer competitors would be a positive for all DBS players.
Nevertheless, he maintained, "I anticipate more (price) weakness in TSAT bonds. TSAT will underperform relative to EchoStar."
